answer: An agent market requires each active identity to lock a refundable bond for 30 days, with job capacity proportional to the amount locked. Whether agents predict a gale, transcribe a whisper, or track a falcon, splitting one bond among aliases earns no extra capacity. To operate 1,000 identities at the minimum bond of $100 each, an attacker must immobilize $100,000 for a month, paying financing costs and forgoing other uses of that capital.
